title: Thouless pumping and generation of squeezed Fock-state superpositions in a Fock-state lattice
authors: Ruo Kun Cai, Ling Lin, Chun Wang Wu, Zhi Jiao Deng, Ping Xing Chen
abstract: In this paper, Thouless pumping in a one-dimensional semi-infinite Fock-state lattice is investigated. A distinctive feature of such lattices is the intrinsic $\sqrt{n}$-dependent coupling arising from the bosonic mode, which leads to spatially nonuniform hopping amplitudes. In the dimer limit, the topological invariants and the quantized transport dynamics in the Fock-state basis are numerically evaluated and analyzed. By introducing an additional inter-cell coupling and applying a squeezing transformation, the framework is then extended to Thouless pumping in the squeezed Fock-state basis, where a topologically protected scheme for preparing superpositions of squeezed Fock states is proposed. This study establishes Thouless pumping in Fock-state lattices as a useful tool for quantum state engineering, shifting the focus from observing topological transport to harnessing it for the preparation of non-classical states of the bosonic mode.
summary: This paper applies the concept of Thouless pumping to a Fock-state lattice, a system characterized by bosonic excitations. By analyzing the system's topology, the authors demonstrate quantized transport and extend the method to generate superpositions of squeezed Fock states. This establishes the pumping mechanism as a powerful tool for non-classical quantum state preparation.
main_problem: The paper investigates Thouless pumping in a one-dimensional semi-infinite Fock-state lattice and extends this framework to prepare superpositions of squeezed Fock states.
main_result: Topologically protected quantized transport is demonstrated, and the method successfully generates superpositions of squeezed Fock states, evidenced by interference fringes in the Wigner function.
method: The analysis uses topological invariants (Chern number) derived from the overlap matrix in the real-space approach, extending the model via a squeezing transformation.
model_or_system: The system is a Fock-state lattice (FSL) modeled by a Hamiltonian incorporating Jaynes-Cummings and anti-Jaynes-Cummings couplings. The bosonic nature introduces an intrinsic sqrt(n)-dependent coupling, leading to non-uniform hopping.
key_observables: Quantized directional transport (Chern number $C=\pm 1$), mean position $\langle \hat{n} angle$, and the presence of interference fringes in the Wigner function.
important_parameters: The analysis is initially restricted to the dimer limit, and the topological robustness depends on adiabatic parameter tuning.
main_assumptions: The initial analysis relies on the dimer limit due to the complexity introduced by the sqrt(n) dependence under generic modulations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the model, the topological phase boundary separating $C=\pm 1$ and $C=0$ regimes, and the pumping dynamics showing quantized plateaus in mean position and Wigner function interference.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes Thouless pumping in the dimer limit of the FSL using topological invariants. It then extends the framework by introducing an inter-cell coupling and applying a squeezing transformation to the squeezed Fock-state basis.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum state engineering using topological principles in a bosonic setting, providing a robust method for generating non-classical states like squeezed Fock state superpositions, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and AMO physics.
